questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)=2\operatorname{tan}⁡t,$ we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2{sec}^{2}⁡t,
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=2{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=2{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}=4.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡t,$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})=\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=\sqrt{2}\cdot 1=\sqrt{2}.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨{x}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,\sqrt{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=4{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}-1,$ we have

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(1)=12\cdot {1}^{2}+6\cdot 1=18.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(1) & =⟨{x}^{′}(1),\,{y}^{′}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,18⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)=\sqrt{1-t},$ we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-t}},
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(-1)=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-(-1)}}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=3{t}^{2},$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=6t,
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(-1)=6(-1)=-6.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(-1) & =⟨{x}^{′}(-1),\,{y}^{′}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}},\,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|{r}^{′}(-1)| & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}})}^{2}+{(-6)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{8}+36} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{289}{8}} \\  & =\frac{17\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the derivative of  $f(t)=({e}^{t}+\operatorname{tan}⁡t)\,i-5\,j+{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,k$ with respect to $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
We find the derivative of $f(t)$  by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}+\operatorname{tan}⁡t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)k \\  & =({e}^{t}+{sec}^{2}⁡t)\,i-0\,j+(2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+t)\,k \\  & =({e}^{t}+{sec}^{2}⁡t)\,i+(2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.problem: Calculate the second derivative of  $f(s)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡2s,\,{s}^{4}+10s,\,55⟩$ with respect to $s.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}({s}^{4}+10s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(55)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2s,\,4{s}^{3}+10,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the second derivative by differentiating ${f}^{′}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4{s}^{3}+10),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2s,\,12{s}^{2},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Second Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
questions.problem: Find the second derivative of $f(t)=t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+(\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})\,k$ with respect to $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+(3\cdot \frac{1}{3}{t}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}t)\,k \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+({t}^{2}-t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)\,k \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+(2t-1)\,k \\  & =-(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+(2t-1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the second derivative of $f(t)=2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{e}^{t})\,j+(2{t}^{3}+t-2)\,k$ with respect to $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{e}^{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+t-2)\,k \\  & =\frac{2}{t}\,i-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{t})\,j+(6{t}^{2}+1)\,k \\  & =\frac{2}{t}\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-{e}^{t})\,j+(6{t}^{2}+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

  

Then, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-{e}^{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}+1)\,k \\  & =-\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}\,i+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{t})\,j+12t\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Second Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
questions.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡(2t),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =2\operatorname{tan}⁡(2t)\operatorname{sec}⁡(2t) \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =4\operatorname{sec}⁡(2t){tan}^{2}⁡(2t)+4\operatorname{sec}⁡(2t){sec}^{2}⁡(2t) \\  & =4\operatorname{sec}⁡(2t)({tan}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sec}^{2}⁡(2t)).\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{3}),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =\frac{3}{t} \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{sec}⁡(2t)({tan}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sec}^{2}⁡(2t)),\,-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \langle 10t^4 ,\, 6\ln t\rangle,$ what is $\mathbf r'\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t) = 10t^4,$ we have

$$
x'(t) = 40t^3,
$$

and therefore

$$
x'\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 40\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = 5.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t) = 6 \ln t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t)=\frac{6}{t},\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
y'\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{6}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}=12.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨{x}^{′}(\frac{1}{2}),\,{y}^{′}(\frac{1}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨5,\,12⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the derivative of  $\mathbf f(t) = \langle \sin t ,\cos t , t \rangle$ at $t= \dfrac{\pi}4.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $\mathbf f'(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute $\mathbf f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}4\right),$ we substitute $t=\dfrac{\pi}4$ into the expression for $\mathbf f'(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: The Second Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t^6,\, t^5\rangle,$ Calculate $\mathbf r''(t).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t) = t^6,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =6{t}^{5} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =30{t}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t) = t^5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =5{t}^{4} \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =20{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨30{t}^{4},\,20{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =10⟨3{t}^{4},\,2{t}^{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
